label: prop:habiro-precision-ladder-equivalence
title: Precision-ladder coefficients are Habiro integer evaluations
html:
For a braid word T_w write u = q^{1/2} and \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w, q) = p_w(u)/d_w(u) in lowest terms, with p_w, d_w \in \mathbb{Z}[u]. The trace itself is not a polynomial in u: at z = q^3/(q^2+1), \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = z = u^6/(u^4+1). The denominator-cleared numerator p_w admits a finite Habiro expansion with integer coefficients,

  p_w(u) \;=\; \sum_{m=0}^{M} a_m(u) \cdot (u;\,u)_m,
  \qquad
  a_m \in \mathbb{Z}[u],
  \qquad M < \infty,

where (u;\,u)_m = \prod_{k=1}^{m}(1-u^{k}) is the q-Pochhammer symbol. It is an exact, finite rational evaluation, not a truncated series.

For the neutron–proton difference the expansion is applied to the numerator of \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_n) - \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_p) over a common denominator. Subtracting the two coefficient lists directly is not valid at z = q^3/(q^2+1), because the denominators differ: d_p = 4u^{18}(u^4+1)^2 and d_n = 4u^{18}.

Under the archimedean evaluation u \mapsto u_0 at the substrate square-root, each (u_0;\,u_0)_m with m \ll 1/(u_0 - 1) \approx 19 contributes a factor that shrinks like \sim \hbar_q^m, where \hbar_q is the universal substrate Planck quantum (categorical; the exact algebraic values at the substrate q_0 are not reproduced here).

The verified proton Habiro coefficients, the uniqueness of the archimedean evaluation, and the scope of the exact evaluation are collected in the Habiro precision-ladder context.

Archimedean specialisation. The Habiro / precision-ladder Taylor coefficients (\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}) are the real archimedean evaluations of the generic Habiro-ring expansion; the real coefficient sequences sit on the archimedean side of the substrate wall, acknowledged here.
